With size=128, the original processes all indices 0-127, but the mutant only processes 0-126. When the last element has a positive hinge loss margin (i.e., 1 - predictions[127]*targets[127] > 0), the original includes it in the sum but the mutant does not. The final loss is divided by size=128 in both cases, so the difference equals margin[127]/128. This is detectable when the last element has a sufficiently large margin contribution.

rounds.recommendations: When implementing boundary guards in GPU kernels, always test edge cases where the boundary condition directly affects the last valid element. Include tests that isolate contributions from boundary elements to catch off-by-one errors in index comparisons.

def generate_inputs(device):
    # All elements: predictions*targets >= 1 so margin <= 0 (no contribution)
    predictions = torch.ones(128, 1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    targets = torch.ones(128, 1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    # Last element: predictions*targets = -100, margin = 1-(-100) = 101
    predictions[127, 0] = -100.0
    targets[127, 0] = 1.0
    return [predictions, targets]
